$schema-note: Design tokens for MrBinnacle/skills. Transcribed from the MrBinnacle repositories Brand Kit v0.1 (2026-08-11). This file is the repository-local source of truth: the kit is the origin, this is what ships. Each repository keeps its own token file on purpose - a shared file would make one repository a build dependency of another.

source.authority: Live repository facts and project-locked decisions outrank this file. This file outranks historical design packets.

color.$note: The green palette from the owner's design pack (mrbinnacle-skills-design-system.zip, exported 2026-10-07), adopted 2026-10-15 (#366, built under #423). It replaced the field palette and its repo.*, light.*, field.* and accent.light/dark tokens, which have no replacement. Values with no green name are derived by the pack.

green-100.role: Primitive, lightest. The retired state mark on light

green-200.role: Primitive. Muted text and the accent on light

green-300.role: Primitive. Hairlines on dark, the turned-away state mark on light

green-400.role: Primitive. Dark surface, the admitted state mark on light

green-500.role: Primitive, darkest. Dark backdrop, ink on light

structural.$note: Dark scheme. Contrast measured 2026-10-16 (WCAG 2 relative luminance): ink 12.96 on bg, 10.87 on surface; muted 7.18, 6.02; accent 5.58, 4.68; line 1.86, 1.56 (under 3:1 by design).

structural_light.$note: Light scheme, composed on its own rather than inverted. Contrast measured 2026-10-16: ink 14.78 on bg, 13.35 on surface; muted 5.75, 5.19; accent 5.75, 5.19; line 1.83, 1.65 (under 3:1 by design).

accent.on_light.role: The one accent on light: the :focus-visible outline and the :hover underline only. Never text, never a fill, never a state

accent.on_dark.role: The one accent on dark: the :focus-visible outline and the :hover underline only. Never text, never a fill, never a state

state.$note: Each state has a light and a dark mark. A mark only; the state must also read as text or shape.

usage_rules: At least 80 percent of any asset stays neutral.
One accent per composition, on focus and hover only. The accent never fills an area and never marks a state.

No colour the sibling instrument declares belongs to this set (its retired #3FB950, #D29922 and #58A6FF, and its current accent #ADB78C). No colour here reads as a success, measured or verdict state: kept is not measured. The palette is a desaturated green-grey neutral family; no value in it is a saturated success green, and none marks a verdict.

declared_hex_surfaces.$note: Which files the declared-hex check reads, stated as data for the same reason copy.words_to_avoid_surfaces is: widening a scanned surface is a decision, not a maintenance task, and a glob hard-coded in the script hides that decision inside a diff. Until 2026-09-07 the check read assets/*.svg only, so site/style.css drew every colour from this file with nothing verifying it (MrBinnacle/skills#256). A colour reaches a reader through the stylesheet exactly as it does through an asset. Kinds: svg_hex parses the SVG and reads fill/stroke/stop-color and style blocks; css_hex reads the stylesheet with comments removed, because a hex inside /* */ ships no colour; raster_icon decodes a PNG and checks every opaque pixel against the colours the entry lists (#448).

surfaces.why: A rendered graphic ships its colours literally. This surface is the original declared-hex check.
The landing page stylesheet. Every value in it is drawn from this token file, and before #256 nothing checked that.

The 32-pixel favicon, rendered from assets/favicon.svg under its default (light) rule: structural_light.ink on a transparent ground. A PNG carries no hex, so each opaque pixel (alpha 128 or more) must lie within tolerance per channel of a listed colour. On a transparent ground an anti-aliased pixel keeps the ink's own colour, so the ink is the whole list. Before #448 no check read a PNG, and this icon kept the retired ink #1F2328, which sits 8 from #1E2020 in blue. The tolerance of 3 covers the rounding of the current render (at most 2) and refuses that ink.

The 180-pixel Apple touch icon, rendered from assets/favicon.svg under its default (light) rule: structural_light.ink on structural_light.bg. A touch icon needs an opaque ground, and the light rule's ink pairs with the light scheme's bg. Anti-aliased edges and the glyph's 0.55-opacity strokes are opaque blends of the two, so each opaque pixel must lie within tolerance per channel of a listed colour or of an 8-bit blend of the two. Before #448 this icon kept a #FFFFFF ground (16 from #F2F4EF in blue) and the retired ink #1F2328 (4 from the nearest blend). The current render deviates by at most 1.

type.$note: IBM Plex, self-hosted from IBM's unmodified Latin1 woff2 files (@ibm/plex-sans 1.1.0, @ibm/plex-mono 2.5.0, SIL OFL 1.1, Reserved Font Name 'Plex'), so the files are never subset or converted here. Adopted 2026-10-15 (#366, built under #423). Surfaces that cannot load the site's @font-face, such as an SVG behind , fall back to the system fonts in each stack.
type.font.mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", Consolas, monospace

roles.Plex Mono 500: State labels, counts, commands, identifiers, evidence values, project descriptors

rules: Uppercase only for compact labels, maker's marks, and short warnings.
Body line length 65 to 75 characters on web surfaces.
No stencil, slab, or condensed display face as a default.
1px rules rather than shadows to separate regions.
No gradients, glows, blurs, glassmorphism, parallax, or decorative motion.

construction.MRBINNACLE: IBM Plex Sans, 700, uppercase, tight tracking

wordmark.compact_mark_retired: The MB compact mark left the repo identity by owner ruling (2026-08-23, skill-harness #216): it is a personal mark, and this repository is not positioned around its owner. The receipt glyph in the banners is the repo's semantic mark; no replacement mark is to be manufactured.
wordmark.clear_space: width of the M on every side

asset_pairs.$note: Files that must change together, read at runtime by scripts/validate_brand_kit.py. The social preview ships as a text-bearing SVG source plus an exported raster. Only the source has a text layer a copy check can read, so an edit to the source that is not re-exported would leave the copy check certifying text no stranger sees. Each pair records the sha256 of both files; either one drifting from its recorded hash is refused, which makes re-recording a deliberate two-file act.
asset_pairs.pairs_pending: None. The one remaining step for the social preview is the upload to the repository's social-preview setting, which is the owner's web-UI act and which no check in this repository can observe.
asset_pairs.recording_procedure: python scripts/validate_brand_kit.py --record-hashes rewrites every recorded hash from the files on disk. Run it only after both halves of a pair are updated.

social_preview.structure: one lockup, one statement, one supporting state or count
social_preview.counts_rule: The counts must be regenerated from live repository state before export.

words_to_avoid_digest.$note: The sha256 of the WORD LIST, not of this file: sha256(json.dumps(copy.words_to_avoid, separators=(",",":")).encode()). MrBinnacle/skill-harness#462 vendors the list and compares its copy against this value. The digest is taken over the list because a file-level digest changes on every unrelated edit here - a colour value, a recorded pair hash, a note like this one - and a drift contract that reddens for reasons its reader cannot act on gets muted. This value changes when the list changes and at no other time. scripts/validate_brand_kit.py recomputes it on every run and refuses a disagreement; --record-digest rewrites it.

copy.words_to_avoid_scope: Every line of prose this repository publishes, and every public asset copy surface with it: social previews, the repository description, release art, and any rendered graphic. Two documents stand outside it and are named in words_to_avoid_surfaces below. Operator ruling, 2026-09-06: one word list, every repository, every line of prose, same rules. Selection is the tracked set (#267, 2026-09-07): every surface glob below is intersected with `git ls-files --cached`, so a file the working tree holds and git does not track is out of scope. The repository publishes what it tracks. When git cannot name the tracked set the checker refuses rather than scanning something else; the reasoning is in scripts/validate_brand_kit.py.

words_to_avoid_surfaces.$note: The machine-readable half of words_to_avoid_scope, read at runtime by scripts/validate_brand_kit.py. The prose above states the rule for a human; this states it for the check, and the two must agree. Until 2026-09-07 this note said README BODY prose was deliberately absent because banned words appear there on purpose. The operator ruling of 2026-09-06 superseded that sentence: one word list, all repositories, every single line of prose, the same rules. The markdown_prose surface below carries the ruling. Two exclusions survive it and each has a reason the ruling does not overturn. _quarantine/** holds frozen candidates, so a rule that reddened on one would demand an edit this repository forbids. CHANGELOG.md records what shipped under the wording in force at the time, so rewriting an entry would falsify the record the file exists to keep. Adding any further surface here is still a decision rather than a maintenance task: it changes what the repository refuses.

surfaces.why: A rendered graphic. Copy is the aria-label attributes plus the text content of text, title and desc elements - an accessible label is public copy a screen reader speaks, so a check blind to it is blind to half the surface.

README headings. This surface is now a subset of markdown_prose below, which reaches the whole file under the ruling of 2026-09-06; a heading breach therefore reports under both labels. It survives the widening for one mechanical reason: scripts/validate_vale_style.py refuses a Vale rule bound to any glob this file does not declare, and .vale.ini binds [README.md]. Dropping this entry would fail that check. It also states a real emphasis - a heading is the copy a stranger skims - and reporting twice is stricter, not weaker.

Every line of prose the repository publishes, under the ruling of 2026-09-06. Copy is the whole document with fenced code blocks removed: a fence holds commands, JSON and file listings, where a banned word can be the name of a real thing rather than a claim about it. README headings sit inside this surface as well as inside the markdown_headings surface above, so a banned word in a README heading is reported twice, once per surface. The narrower surface is kept because .vale.ini binds the fast Vale feedback to that exact glob and scripts/validate_vale_style.py refuses any binding to a glob this list does not declare.
The repository description. The forge's own description field is a web setting no check can read; this is the repository-local surface it is written from.

The landing page at mrbinnacle.github.io/skills, the first page a stranger reads. Copy is the rendered text plus the aria-label, alt and title attributes and the description and title meta content; script and style bodies and comments are not copy. The page sat outside every copy check until 2026-10-23, which is how a sentence ledger row C2 forbids stayed on it.

words_to_avoid_notes.$note: Historical context only. A note here NEVER grants a permission: the checkers ban every word in words_to_avoid flat, and scripts/test_validate_brand_kit.py refuses a note that reads as a permission unless a checker reads this object and branches on that word. The 'robust' and 'production-ready' entries removed on 2026-09-07 said 'Permitted only when...' and 'Permitted only with proof attached', which neither checker implemented (MrBinnacle/skills#265). Neither word had ever been used in prose in either public repository, so the permission was never exercised. To grant one, build the branch first.
words_to_avoid_notes.earn: This repository retired the tagline 'skills that have to earn their keep' from three text surfaces. It survived on assets/social-preview.png, which is the one surface a stranger sees before clicking.

rejection_checklist: Does it look like generic AI or developer-tool marketing?
Does it use a claim, count, output, or status not present in repository evidence?
Does it imply a kept skill has been empirically proven?
Does it confuse inventory state with measurement state?
Is chromatic color decorative rather than semantic?
Does texture reduce the legibility of evidence?
Are shadows, gradients, glows, glass, or floating cards building the hierarchy?
Is an icon being used as decoration without meaning?
Could the asset belong to any AI startup after changing the wordmark?
Does the copy sound more polished but less like Matthew?

known_gaps.note: Measured against the committed assets on 2026-09-06, not assumed. Every gap recorded here since 2026-08-12 is closed; each closure is a receipt under closed_gaps below. A new gap is recorded here with the ticket that closes it.

closed_gaps.$note: Kept rather than deleted. A gap that was recorded, then closed, is a receipt; deleting the record leaves no way to tell a closed gap from one that was never noticed.

social_preview_raster_is_unreadable.was: assets/social-preview.png was a raster with no text layer. No check could read its copy or its colours, so both were asserted by eye. It carried the retired tagline 'skills that have to earn their keep' and #3fb950 (measured 2026-08-30: 3,420 exact solid fills over all 819,200 pixels), and it is the one surface a stranger sees before clicking.
social_preview_raster_is_unreadable.how: The raster is now an export of assets/social-preview.svg, the text-bearing source checked in 2026-08-30 (MrBinnacle/skills#62), rendered at 1280x640 by hand at build (the renderer stays out of CI, DESIGN.md). The source's copy sits inside words_to_avoid_surfaces, and the two files are recorded as a pair under asset_pairs with the sha256 of each, so a source edit that is not re-exported is refused. The export was scanned after rendering: zero #3fb950 pixels. The upload to the repository setting remains the owner's act.

compact_mark_still_in_the_lockups.was: wordmark.compact_mark_retired records that the MB compact mark left the repo identity on 2026-08-23. assets/lockup-horizontal.svg and assets/lockup-stacked.svg still drew it.
compact_mark_still_in_the_lockups.how: Both lockups now draw the receipt glyph, in the two banners' own path data, at 28px mark height in the clear-space geometry the files already declared. No replacement mark was manufactured: the receipt glyph is the mark wordmark.compact_mark_retired names. The wordmark text runs and the aria-label are unchanged; colour stays currentColor, with the banners' muted-over-ink relationship carried by stroke-opacity so neither file declares a hex.

no_light_mode_neutrals.was: The kit defined structural neutrals for dark surfaces only. assets/banner-light.svg shipped #1f2328, #57606a and #2da44e, none declared anywhere in the kit.
no_light_mode_neutrals.how: color.structural_light declares the light counterpart of the dark primitive set. #2da44e was removed from the asset rather than declared - see the next entry.

instrument_green_on_inventory_assets.was: assets/banner-dark.svg used #3fb950 (harness.prompt) and assets/banner-light.svg used #2da44e for the same receipt-seal accent. The inventory was wearing the test bench's palette on both.
instrument_green_on_inventory_assets.how: Both banners now draw the stamped line and seal in a declared structural neutral - repo.muted on dark, light.muted on light. No accent was substituted: replacing a borrowed hex with a newly minted one would close the gap by inventing a token. assets/social-preview.png still carries #3fb950 (measured 2026-08-30; the #2da44e this entry previously asserted occurs zero times in the raster) and is tracked as an open gap above.

site_icons_on_the_retired_palette.was: site/favicon-32.png and site/apple-touch-icon.png were last rendered on 2026-09-06 (#257), before #429 retired the field palette. Measured by the #443 surface audit: every full-alpha favicon pixel was the retired ink #1F2328, and the touch icon drew that ink on a #FFFFFF ground. This file declared surfaces of kind svg_hex and css_hex only, so no check read a PNG and scripts/validate_brand_kit.py reported PASS (MrBinnacle/skills#448).
site_icons_on_the_retired_palette.how: Both icons were re-rendered from assets/favicon.svg under its default (light) rule with headless Chrome, by hand at build: the renderer stays out of CI (DESIGN.md). The touch icon's ground is structural_light.bg #F2F4EF, the light scheme's backdrop for the light rule's ink #1E2020. color.declared_hex_surfaces gained the raster_icon kind and one entry per icon, and the new check was shown naming both old files before the re-render. The uploaded GitHub social preview is a separate owner act (#481).

not_enforced.was: Nothing read this file. A check asserting every hex in assets/*.svg is declared here would have failed on both banners.
not_enforced.how: scripts/validate_brand_kit.py reads this file and runs three checks over it: banned copy on the surfaces named in copy.words_to_avoid_surfaces, hash agreement on the files named in asset_pairs, and every hex in assets/*.svg declared here. It runs in .github/workflows/tests.yml on both operating-system cells, with a poison control per assertion. It GATES: the protect-main ruleset lists validator (ubuntu-latest) and validator (windows-latest) among the required status checks on main, so a nonzero exit blocks the merge. A green run is compliance, not silence. Read the ruleset to check this, not repos/MrBinnacle/skills/branches/main/protection: the legacy endpoint does not report rulesets and answers 404 Branch not protected for a branch a ruleset protects.

evidence_rules: Every number must resolve to a repository artifact.
Never invent waveform traces, terminal output, sample verdicts, user counts, stars, testimonials, or performance metrics.
If a visual requires unavailable evidence, show an empty state or omit it.
Do not let KEPT visually imply empirically proven. Admission state and measurement state stay separate.

public_claims.$note: Wording docs/product/claims-ledger.md forbids on a public surface, read at runtime by scripts/validate_brand_kit.py. The ledger states the rule for a human; this states it for the check. Each pattern carries must_match and must_not_match examples, and the checker refuses a pattern that misses its own forbidden example or catches its own allowed one. The surfaces are the public ones only: internal records such as PRODUCT.md may state the internal direction (#547 ruling, 2026-10-20). Added 2026-10-23 after the C2 sentence was found on the landing page.

patterns.why: Pi is the direction, not a delivered runtime. A public surface may not call it the primary, first or main runtime.
must_match: Pi is the runtime this work targets first.
must_not_match: There is no tested Pi install yet.
The install below is for Claude Code. An install for Pi, another coding agent, is planned and untested.
